title: fix(cron): scheduled automations run on whatever runtime their session copies instead of the one they were bound for
body:
Related: #178812

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled automation's runtime is decided at run time from whatever runtime override its cron session copies, not from what the job was created with. A job created from a conversation that runs Claude through `claude-cli` was bound to an account chosen for the embedded runtime, then ran on the CLI. On 2026-10-20, before #180492, that failed twice with "Automation candidate is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route". Since #180492, a forwarding CLI accepts the account, but the runtime still follows the copied override on each run. The error also didn't say which account or runtime was involved.

A related failure on 2026-10-25: an hourly automation with no recorded account failed 10 times in a row after the default model moved to a provider with a stored profile. The message ("Automation has no recorded inference account…") named neither the account nor the runtime, so it was unclear what to record.

## User Impact

User impact: new automations record the runtime they will run on next to their account, and every run executes on that runtime. **The account is unchanged:** capture binds exactly the account it bound before this PR, so nothing changes who pays for a run. A job created from a `claude-cli` conversation records that account with `runtime: "claude-cli"`, and claude-cli keeps receiving it, as #180492 does today. A job bound for the embedded runtime stays embedded, even if its cron session later copies a different runtime override.

- Errors name what's wrong. A bound job whose account was removed fails with `Automation inference account <profile> on runtime <runtime> was removed or signed out…`. A job with no recorded account fails with `…Runtime <runtime> would run <provider/model> with stored account <profile>. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profile>, or with openclaw doctor --fix.`
- Doctor's existing account-adoption warning now also says the job's runs are refused until it records the account.
- Existing jobs are not migrated. Bindings recorded before this change have no runtime and keep today's resolution, and their errors say `(no recorded runtime)`. Older Gateways ignore the extra field, so a downgrade keeps working.

## Why This Change Was Made

Phase 5 of the scheduled-run execution context (design: "One tuple, one resolver"):
- **One resolver.** `resolveCronCandidateExecution` decides a candidate's runtime and execution route. It's shared by inference capture and every scheduled-run candidate, so the two can't disagree for the same inputs.
- **Capture records the tuple.** Account selection is unchanged from main. Capture adds the runtime, resolved from the same entry the cron session will copy: the target row for `session:` jobs, or the runtime the creating conversation carries for `current` jobs. That carry rule is extracted from `isolated-agent/session.ts` unchanged, so both sides use one rule. Capture stores the result as `runtime` on the binding.
- **Runs use the captured runtime.** On detached runs and on `session:` jobs (the shared reply path), run preparation, harness selection and candidate dispatch read the binding's runtime instead of the session's override.
- **Account edits keep the runtime.** `automations edit --model <ref>@<profile>` records the new account with the job's existing runtime. If that runtime is no longer available for the same provider, the edit is rejected and the stored binding stays unchanged, so an edit never silently moves a job to another runtime. An edit to an unbound or legacy job resolves the runtime the same way create does.
- **One drift guard.** `assertCandidate` refuses a candidate whose provider or runtime differs from the binding, naming both. The unrecorded-account refusal now has one helper, shared by the embedded auth plan, the cron CLI path, the reply-path CLI candidate and CLI preparation.

Deferred to openclaw-84c: Codex app authority (row N1) still reads `trigger` and `scheduledRuntimeAuthority`. Moving it to `ScheduledExecutionFacts` needs the same plugin SDK harness facts contract as rows 41/43. Behavior is the same either way.

## Evidence

**Crabbox (AWS), head `943f9065578`:** (`12df361d7fc` changes only the dev replay script `scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts` and its test, which this Gateway proof does not run.)

| | |
|---|---|
| Command | `CRABBOX_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 CRABBOX_CAPACITY_REGIONS=us-east-1,us-east-2,us-west-2 crabbox run --provider aws --ttl 75m --timing-json --download proof-out.tgz=… --shell -- "bash proof/0d513-remote.sh"` (host `OPENCLAW_*` variables unset) |
| Tested source | The box syncs the working tree onto its seed commit, so it reports `543c92ba688` as git HEAD. SHA-256 of all 26 changed files on the box matches local head `943f9065578e0ec3d0ca79ac752da5c3d8cd89fb`. The proof scripts, mock endpoint and QA CLI plugin are local tooling and are not committed. |
| Provider / lease | `aws`, `c7a.8xlarge`, lease `cbx_8afa4291833a`, stopped; inspect reports `"state":"released"` |
| Run | [run_65e166a15062952a84c2219a677fa022](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_65e166a15062952a84c2219a677fa022), exit 0 |

Real Gateway upgrade proof. v2026.10.7 (latest stable) creates state, then this build runs it. The provider is a mock OpenAI-compatible endpoint `qa-proof/m1` with a stored API key `qa-proof:manual`. A QA plugin registers `qa-proof-cli`, a CLI backend for that provider that does not forward stored accounts. 12/12 assertions passed:

1. **v2026.10.7 (latest stable)** stores `qa-proof:manual` and creates an isolated job. Stable releases record no binding.
2. **This build, no migration:** the stored job is unchanged. Its run is refused with `Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime openclaw would run qa-proof/m1 with stored account qa-proof:manual. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model qa-proof/m1@qa-proof:manual, or with openclaw doctor --fix.` This is the 2026-10-25 shape.
3. **Doctor** previews `retain qa-proof:manual for qa-proof/m1 … Its runs are refused until it records this account.` `doctor --fix` records the binding without a runtime, and the job then runs embedded (`QA-PROOF-EMBEDDED-REPLY`). Existing jobs keep today's resolution.
4. **Conversation on a CLI runtime:** a conversation on `qa-proof/m1` with `agentRuntimeOverride: qa-proof-cli`. A `current` job created from it binds `qa-proof:manual`, the same account main binds, now with `runtime: "qa-proof-cli"`. This backend can't use a stored account, so the run is refused as it is on main. The message now names the account and the runtime: `…incompatible with its recorded inference account and route (account qa-proof:manual on runtime qa-proof-cli). The selected runtime uses a CLI login that cannot use this job's stored account…`. A new isolated job records `runtime: "openclaw"` and runs embedded.
5. **Drift guard:** after `models.authLogout` removes `qa-proof:manual`, the new bound job fails with `Automation inference account qa-proof:manual on runtime openclaw was removed or signed out…`. The Doctor-bound job fails with `…qa-proof:manual (no recorded runtime) was removed…`, and the CLI-runtime job fails with `…qa-proof:manual on runtime qa-proof-cli was removed…`.

The same box ran the focused tests: propagation, binding normalization, context fixtures, auth-continuity integration, Doctor migration and gateway `cron.inference-binding`. 7 files, 138 tests passed, including the shared-session reply-path suite.

**Focused tests** (`src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts`):
- A `current` job from a `claude-cli` creator, on an Anthropic model, with a stored Anthropic API key, binds that API key, as main does, with `runtime: "claude-cli"`. claude-cli receives the key. With a stored Anthropic token, it records that token the same way.
- **A binding recorded without a runtime resolves exactly as before:** with the same copied `claude-cli` override, it runs on claude-cli with the bound account.
- **`session:` job on the shared reply path:** the target row carries `agentRuntimeOverride: "claude-cli"` and the binding records `openclaw`. Candidates resolve and are checked on `openclaw`, and the run is embedded (`agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts`).
- **Account edit:** a job recorded on `claude-cli` keeps `runtime: "claude-cli"` after `--model …@<profile>`, even though config alone would pick the embedded runtime. When that recorded runtime is no longer a CLI backend, the same edit is rejected with `runs on runtime claude-cli, which is unavailable…` and the binding is left as it was.
- These tests fail with their fix reverted and pass with it.
- The unrecorded-account refusal text is pinned in full on the embedded path (`isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts`, real runner) and on the CLI path.
- A bound job captured for the embedded runtime runs embedded even when its cron session copies `agentRuntimeOverride: "claude-cli"`. It also stays embedded when config later moves its model to a CLI runtime.
- A bound `claude-cli` job whose runtime is no longer a CLI backend fails with `account … on runtime claude-cli` and `captured for runtime claude-cli`.
- A removed account fails embedded and CLI candidates with one message naming the account and the captured runtime.

**Static replay** (`scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts` on Josh's Gateway, read-only copies, at `6e4ae6c0f67`; from `12df361d7fc` the replay picks each bound job's model through `resolveCronModelSelection`, the owner capture and runs use, and reports `inference runtime unresolved` instead of guessing when that selection fails or leaves the bound provider): Rerun at `12df361d7fc`: 108 jobs, all 39 bound jobs report `inference runtime unresolved`, because the selection owner refuses this Gateway's agent databases (schema 35; this checkout expects 37 until Doctor upgrades them). No inference label is guessed. The figures below are from the earlier head. 108 jobs. The new `inference` field: 31 bound jobs `equal`, 77 unbound or runtime-owned with no label. **No `gain-unexpected` on any field.** Every stored binding predates the `runtime` field and keeps the runtime its run picks today. The remaining `loss` labels (`automationsCli`, `requesterYield`, `ownerEmbedded`) and the pauses come from earlier phases and are explained in #183987 and #183913.

Pinned fixtures for this phase:
- `equal`: bound with `runtime: "claude-cli"` (same account as main), and the run would pick claude-cli from the copied override. This is the #180492 shape.
- `equal`: bound without a runtime, run copies a CLI override. It resolves as today.
- `retarget`: bound with `runtime: "claude-cli"`, but the conversation's override has since changed to the embedded runtime. Named cause: the job stays on its captured runtime instead of following the creator.

**Local:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files pass. Autoreview found no P0/P1 issues. It used Claude, because the Codex CLI failed authentication on this host.
